title: General Ledger
subtitle: Setting up revenue mapping for automatic GL generation

intro.title: Finance & Accounting: General Ledger Setup
lines: This picks up after your GL library is built —
the chart of accounts below.
Next: map revenue accounts for automatic GL generation.
intro.narration: This video is for finance and accounting teams. It picks up after you've already built your GL library — your chart of accounts, shown here — and walks through how to map revenue accounts so the general ledger generates seamlessly on its own.

steps.title: Default Accounts
lines: Sets standard revenue accounts by payment method,
plus the org-wide Deferred Revenue account.
steps.narration: Default Accounts sets your standard revenue accounts by payment method, and — importantly — the Deferred Revenue account. That's the account used any time a revenue type is set to recognize revenue at time of service delivery.

steps.title: General Ledger Settings
lines: Every revenue type — Registrations, Facility Rentals,
Memberships, Events, and more — has its own mapping.
steps.narration: The General Ledger settings page lists every revenue type: Registrations, Facility Rentals, Memberships, Events, and more. Each one gets its own default GL code and its own revenue recognition setting. Let's look at a few.

steps.title: Registrations · Service Delivery
lines: Program enrollments default to the Programs GL code.
Recognized at time of service delivery —
deferred at purchase, recognized as each session runs.
steps.narration: Registrations — program enrollments — default to the Programs GL code, with revenue recognized at time of service delivery. That means revenue is deferred at purchase, then automatically recognized as each session actually takes place.

steps.title: Facility Rentals · Service Delivery
lines: Facility Rentals default to the Facility Rentals GL code,
also recognized at time of service delivery —
deferred until each site reservation.
steps.narration: Facility Rentals work the same way: they default to the Facility Rentals GL code and recognize revenue at service delivery, deferred at purchase and recognized on the date of each site reservation.

steps.title: Memberships · 12-Month Deferral
lines: Also recognized at service delivery.
Deferred Revenue Period defaults to 12 months,
with proration for the first month — adjustable here.
steps.narration: Memberships also recognize revenue at service delivery, and add one more setting: the Deferred Revenue Period. It defaults to twelve months, with proration for that first partial month, and you can adjust it right here.

steps.title: Events · Service Delivery
lines: Recognized when each ticketed event ends.
Splits ticket face value and ticket-service-fee GL codes.
steps.narration: Events recognize revenue when each ticketed event ends, splitting the entry between the ticket face value GL code and the ticket service fee GL code from your finance settings.

steps.title: Example: Program Registration
lines: A $100 registration posts entirely to Deferred Revenue.
Each $10 weekly session then moves $10 out —
into the Programs GL, right on the day it runs.
steps.narration: Here's a real registration: a hundred-dollar purchase posts entirely to Deferred Revenue on day one. Then, automatically, ten dollars moves from Deferred Revenue into the Programs GL account on the day of each weekly session — right on that program's own schedule.

steps.title: Example: Facility Rental
lines: A $450 rental posts to Deferred Revenue at purchase.
$90 moves out on each reservation date —
split across the Facility Rentals and Facility Fees GL.
steps.narration: Same pattern for a facility rental: four hundred fifty dollars posts to Deferred Revenue at purchase. Then ninety dollars moves out on each reservation date, split between the Facility Rentals and Facility Fees GL accounts — right on the day of that site reservation.

steps.title: Example: Membership
lines: A $200 membership prorates a small amount on day one,
then spreads the rest across 12 monthly entries —
moving from Deferred Revenue into the Memberships GL.
steps.narration: And a membership: two hundred dollars posts to Deferred Revenue at purchase, with a small prorated amount recognized that same day for the partial first month. The remaining balance then spreads across twelve monthly entries, moving steadily into the Memberships GL account.

steps.title: General Ledger · All Entries
lines: Every journal entry across your organization,
filterable by date, search, and more.
steps.narration: Clearing the search shows the full General Ledger — every journal entry across your organization, filterable by date and search.

steps.title: General Ledger · Roll-Up
lines: The same entries, totaled by account —
a quick balance check across every GL code.
steps.narration: And the Roll-Up view totals those same entries by account, giving your accounting team a fast balance check across every GL code, for any date range.
